title: Narrative framing record (Phase 6 Step 5)
description: One focused record per canonical article: HOW the article frames political events, issues and actors - the narrative structure, not sentiment. One dominant primary frame (nullable - never forced) plus up to four secondary frames, each carrying the affected entity, an explanation, the political mechanism, who the frame benefits or damages, a verbatim quote and a confidence score. Blame/credit attribution and electoral consequences are OUT of scope for this step by specification.

primary_frame.description: the article's DOMINANT narrative frame; null when the article carries no political framing - never force one

secondary_frames.description: additional genuinely present frames, most salient first

frame_category.description: the specification's frame taxonomy - never invent a category; 'other' requires frame_other_label AND a justification inside the explanation (rule F4)

affected_entity.description: the party / candidate / council / institution the frame is about

explanation.description: how the article constructs this narrative - the audit trail for the frame call

political_mechanism.description: the interpretive route by which this framing could matter politically, AS SUGGESTED BY THE ARTICLE - descriptive only, never an outcome estimate

benefits.description: party/candidate the frame favours, when the article supports saying so; null otherwise

damages.description: party/candidate the frame harms, when the article supports saying so; null otherwise
